title.narrative: IFU India Climate Finance Initiative - capital contribution

description.narrative: Objective: In 2020, Denmark and India formalized a Green Strategic Partnership Agreement. The purpose is to support India’s green transition and strengthen Denmark’s engagement in India. Under this agreement the Danish Minister for Development Cooperation has approved the India Green Investment Initiative, an earmarked capital contribution of DKK 200 million to the Investment Fund for Developing Countries (IFU). The objective is to target green investments in India related to renewable energy, energy efficiency, waste management, and water. This will contribute to the Danish government's target of ensuring that 30% of development assistance under §6.3 of the finance act is green by 2023.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will pay in a capital contribution directly to IFU’s equity over a two-year period with DKK 100 million respectively in 2022 and 2023. With the capital contribution IFU will invest in relevant green projects, while also tolerating a higher risk and possibly a lower return compared to IFU’s SDG Fund. IFU will track and report on progress according to the defined results framework. It is IFU’s expectation that the contribution can mobilize an additional USD 100m through private investors and other development financial institutions for green financing in India.
